title: 고기를 양념에 넣고 나서 30분을 기다립니다
en: Put the meat in the marinade, then wait 30 minutes

items.mean: grilled or roasted dish
items.ex: 이 골목은 생선 구이로 유명합니다.
items.exen: This alley is famous for grilled fish.

items.mean: stir-fried dish
items.ex: 볶음 요리를 맛있게 하려면 기름을 충분히 넣고 센 불에 볶아야 합니다.
items.exen: To make a stir-fry taste good you need plenty of oil and a high flame.

items.mean: steamed or braised dish
items.ex: 저는 찜 요리 중에서 해물찜을 가장 좋아해요.
items.exen: Of all the jjim dishes, seafood jjim is my favourite.

items.mean: deep-fried food, fritters
items.ex: 감자튀김은 아이들 간식으로 인기가 많다.
items.exen: Chips are a popular snack with children.

items.mean: to grill, to roast, to bake (ㅂ irregular → 구워)
items.ex: 겨울에 고구마를 구워 먹으면 맛있어요.
items.exen: Roasted sweet potatoes are delicious in winter.

items.mean: to boil, to make (soup, stew, noodles)
items.ex: 한국에서는 설날에 떡국을 끓여 먹는다.
items.exen: In Korea people make tteokguk on New Year's Day.

items.mean: to trim, to prepare (vegetables, fish) before cooking
items.ex: 요리를 시작하기 전에 채소를 미리 다듬어야 해요.
items.exen: You should trim the vegetables before you start cooking.

items.mean: to mince, to chop finely
items.ex: 한국 음식에는 다진 마늘이 많이 들어갑니다.
items.exen: A lot of Korean food has minced garlic in it.

items.mean: to blanch, to parboil briefly
items.ex: 샤부샤부는 고기와 채소, 해물을 끓는 물에 데쳐서 먹는 요리다.
items.exen: Shabu-shabu is a dish where you blanch meat, vegetables and seafood in boiling water.

items.mean: to stir-fry, to fry in a pan with oil
items.ex: 오징어 볶음을 할 때 오징어보다 채소를 먼저 볶아야 해요.
items.exen: When you make stir-fried squid, fry the vegetables before the squid.

items.mean: to pan-fry in a thin layer (jeon, pancakes)
items.ex: 한국에서는 명절에 여러 종류의 전을 부쳐서 먹는다.
items.exen: On holidays Koreans pan-fry several kinds of jeon.

items.mean: to soak (rice, beans, dried food) in water
items.ex: 밥을 짓기 전에 쌀을 물에 불려야 더 맛이 좋아요.
items.exen: Rice tastes better if you soak it before cooking.

items.mean: to boil something in water (eggs, noodles, meat)
items.ex: 계란을 냄비에 넣고 10분 정도 삶으면 완전히 익는다.
items.exen: Put the eggs in a pot and boil them for about 10 minutes and they cook through.

items.mean: to mix, to stir together
items.ex: 간장에 설탕과 다진 마늘을 넣고 잘 섞어 주세요.
items.exen: Add sugar and minced garlic to the soy sauce and mix it well.

items.mean: to slice, to cut up (ㄹ stem → 썰어, 써니)
items.ex: 김치찌개에 돼지고기를 썰어서 넣으세요.
items.exen: Slice the pork and put it into the kimchi stew.

items.mean: to cook something through, to let it cook until done
items.ex: 감자는 푹 익혀야 부드러워져요.
items.exen: Potatoes have to be cooked right through to go soft.

items.mean: to cut (르 irregular → 잘라서)
items.ex: 어머니는 갈비를 먹기 좋게 잘라서 주셨어요.
items.exen: My mother cut the galbi into easy-to-eat pieces for me.

items.mean: to simmer down in sauce, to braise
items.ex: 생선과 무에 간장을 넣고 조렸어요.
items.exen: I simmered fish and radish in soy sauce.

items.mean: to steam
items.ex: 여름에는 간식으로 옥수수나 감자를 쪄 먹습니다.
items.exen: In summer we steam corn or potatoes for a snack.

items.mean: to deep-fry
items.ex: 튀김은 바삭하게 튀겨야 맛있습니다.
items.exen: Fried food has to be fried until crisp to taste good.

grammar.tag: as much as, to the extent that
grammar.def_ko: 앞에 말한 내용과 비슷한 정도나 한도임을 나타내는 표현. '만큼'은 앞에 말한 내용과 비슷한 정도나 한도임을 나타내는 조사.
grammar.def_en: Shows that something matches the degree, amount or limit of what came before — 'as much as ~', 'to the extent that ~'. After a verb or adjective it is -는 / -(으)ㄴ / -(으)ㄹ 만큼; straight after a noun, 만큼 is a particle and is written joined to the noun (아버지만큼).

ex.en: You see as much as you know. (a saying)

ex.ko: 누구나 일한 만큼 월급을 받아야 해요.
ex.en: Everyone should be paid as much as they worked.
The expectations were high, and the disappointment was just as big.

ex.ko: 리사 씨가 기쁜 만큼 저도 기뻐요.
ex.en: I'm as happy as Lisa is.

ex.ko: 저는 고등학교 때 이미 아버지만큼 키가 컸어요.
ex.en: By high school I was already as tall as my father. (noun + 만큼)
That's a lot of food. Have as much as you can eat.

grammar.info_ko: 동사, 형용사, '이다'와 결합한다. 동사는 시제에 따라 '-는/-은/-을 만큼'을 쓰고, 명사 뒤에는 '만큼'을 붙여 쓴다.
grammar.info_en: Verbs pick the ending by tense: -는 만큼 (present), -(으)ㄴ 만큼 (past), -(으)ㄹ 만큼 (future, or 'enough to'). Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 만큼, except 있다/없다 adjectives, which take -는 만큼 (재미있는 만큼). After a noun, 만큼 attaches directly with no space.

grammar.def_ko: 앞에 오는 말의 행동이 끝난 다음에 뒤의 내용이 일어남을 나타내는 표현.
grammar.def_en: Shows that what follows happens once the first action is finished — 'after ~ing'. The stress is on completion, so it almost always appears as -고 나서, -고 나니(까) or -고 나면.

ex.ko: 먼저 영화를 보고 나서 쇼핑을 합시다.
ex.en: Let's watch the film first and then go shopping.
Now that I've sung, I'm hungry.

ex.ko: 이 책을 읽고 나면 생각이 달라질 거예요.
ex.en: Once you've read this book, your thinking will change.

ex.ko: 글을 잘 읽고 나서 문제를 푸세요.
ex.en: Read the text carefully, then answer the questions.

ex.ko: 계란을 먼저 넣고 나서 밥을 넣고 볶으세요.
ex.en: Put the egg in first, then add the rice and stir-fry it.

grammar.info_ko: 동사와 결합한다. 받침에 관계없이 '-고 나다'를 쓰며, 보통 '-고 나서, -고 나니(까), -고 나면'의 형태로 쓴다.
grammar.info_en: Attaches to verbs, and the form never changes — always -고 나다, with or without a final consonant. Compare -(으)ㄴ 다음에 below (same idea, noun-based) and -자마자 from 7과, which is 'the moment you ~' rather than 'after you've finished ~'.

grammar.def_ko: 어떤 행위를 먼저 한 후에 뒤의 행위를 함을 나타내는 표현.
grammar.def_en: Shows that one action is done first and the next one follows — 'after ~ing'.

ex.ko: 조개를 씻은 다음에 물에 넣고 끓이세요.
ex.en: Wash the clams, then put them in water and boil them.

ex.ko: 숙제를 다 끝낸 다음에 친구를 만났어요.
ex.en: I met my friend after I'd finished all my homework.
After putting the meat in the marinade, you wait 30 minutes.

grammar.info_ko: 동사와 결합한다. 받침이 있으면 '-은 다음에', 받침이 없거나 'ㄹ' 받침이면 '-ㄴ 다음에'를 쓴다.
grammar.info_en: Attaches to verbs: -은 다음에 after a final consonant, -ㄴ 다음에 otherwise (a ㄹ stem drops the ㄹ: 살다 → 산 다음에). -(으)ㄴ 후에 and -(으)ㄴ 뒤에 mean the same thing.
